tagline: Two coasts, hundreds of islands — the Andaman and the Gulf, both built for the water.
summary: Thailand's tourism runs on two distinct island seas: the Andaman coast in the west — Phuket, Phi Phi, Krabi and the Similans — and the Gulf of Thailand in the east, with Koh Samui, Koh Phangan, Koh Tao, and the Koh Chang / Koh Kood archipelago near the Cambodian border. Tens of millions of visitors a year complete island legs on speedboats and ferries. A clean, stabilised foiling tier is the premium layer between the crowded speedboat and the absent on-demand option.
why_marine_mobility: No single city brief tells the Thai story, because it spans two island seas. On the Andaman side, Phuket to Krabi and the Phi Phi run carry enormous volume on speedboats that pound through chop; on the Gulf side, the Koh Samui–Phangan–Tao triangle and the Koh Chang–Koh Kood chain move tourists on ferries and longtails. Navier's Pioneer II foiling tier turns these crossings into smooth, dry, premium glides, matched to a market that already pays for high-end resorts and villas.

demand_signals.label: Andaman visitor volume
demand_signals.note: Phuket, Phi Phi, Krabi and the surrounding islands draw a huge share of Thailand's inbound tourism, nearly all of it requiring island water legs.

demand_signals.label: Gulf island triangle
demand_signals.note: Koh Samui, Koh Phangan and Koh Tao form a high-volume island triangle linked entirely by sea.

demand_signals.label: Premium resort & villa market
demand_signals.note: Phuket, Samui and the Koh Kood / Soneva-tier resorts anchor a mature luxury market whose guests value fast, dry, discreet transfers.

demand_signals.label: Digital-hailing penetration
demand_signals.note: Grab operates deeply across Thai metros and tourist hubs; an in-app sea tier extends that demand curve onto the island water.

use_cases.body: Phuket to Krabi: a ~38-nautical-mile Andaman crossing today run on speedboats — ideal for a smooth, dry, premium foiling tier between two of the coast's largest hubs.
Koh Samui / Koh Phangan to Koh Tao: the Gulf island triangle, ~25–33 nautical miles between hubs, run today on ferries and crowded speedboats.
Koh Chang to Koh Kood: a ~32-nautical-mile eastern-Gulf link to the Soneva-tier resort island, a premium transfer comfortably inside Pioneer II range.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The core crossings — Phuket–Krabi (38 nm), the Samui–Phangan–Tao triangle (25–33 nm), and Koh Chang–Koh Kood (32 nm) — sit inside Pioneer II's 70-nautical-mile range at 30 knots, commercial-ready today.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Longer trunks — mainland gateways out to the further Andaman or Gulf island groups — become Quanta-LR territory (~700 nm hybrid range, H2 2026+) as range comes online.

signature_routes.label: Phuket ↔ Krabi — the marquee Andaman crossing
Koh Tao ↔ Koh Phangan — the Gulf island triangle
Koh Chang ↔ Koh Kood — the eastern-Gulf resort link

transit_planning: For a tourism authority or a super-app: a premium, low-emission water tier that makes the busiest island crossings dry, smooth and weather-resilient on both coasts, and gives luxury resorts a discreet transfer their guests will pay for. Start with the proven Andaman and Gulf corridors on Pioneer II, then extend mainland trunks on Quanta-LR.
competitive_landscape: Island travel today splits between ferries (affordable but slow) and speedboats / longtails (quicker but rough, wet and crowded). There is no on-demand premium tier. Navier's foiling craft is the missing middle: faster than a ferry, smoother and drier than a speedboat, cleaner than both, and reachable in-app — matched to a market already paying for high-end stays.
regulatory_note: Thai domestic maritime transport is regulated by the Marine Department under the Ministry of Transport; passenger operation requires vessel registration and route licensing. The provincial marine offices (e.g. Phuket, Krabi, Surat Thani for the Gulf islands) are natural first touchpoints.
seasonality: The two coasts run on opposite seasons: the Andaman is calmest Nov–Apr (southwest monsoon Jun–Oct brings rough seas and speedboat cancellations), while the Gulf is best Jan–Sep with its wettest window late in the year. A stabilised foiling craft holds its schedule through the chop that grounds smaller boats.

precedents.what: Four Seasons Lake Austin operates an N30 in live luxury-hospitality service — proof of the premium water-shuttle model Navier brings to Thailand's island coasts.
